newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end lower on historic high turnover.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end lower on historic high turnover.

text.p: Taiwan shares roared to a six-year high at the open but late individual and institutional profit-taking sent the index to a lower close on Tuesday on all-time high turnover of T$238.9 billion, brokers said.
The benchmark index ended down 57.07 points or 0.67 percent at 8,460.63, off an intraday high of 8,624.78 that was the market's highest level in nearly seven years.
Turnover soared to T$238.9 billion, breaking the historical record of T$216 billion set on March 16, 1990, as the market was tumbling from its all-time closing high of 12,495.34.
Tuesday's fall followed four consecutive days of gains.
A dramatic rally that has sent the index 80 percent higher since February 1996 has lured thousands of new investors into the market, pushing turnover ever higher, brokers said.
"From old to young, from students to professionals -- stock investment has become a nationwide sport," said Nomura Securities analyst Amy Huang.

Electronics, which surged more than five percent on Monday, encountered heavy profit-taking, at one point plunging more than three percent in intraday trading. Bargain hunters entered to slow the selling and the sector ended down just 0.85 percent.

Computer giant Acer slipped T$3 to T$73.5. Motherboard maker Asustek, the market's high price "king share", fell T$43 to T$700. Bargain hunters snapped up shares in rebounding chipmakers, sending United Microelectronics up the daily seven percent limit to T$65.5.
"Many analysts have mixed views on whether semiconductor shares can recover so strongly as some had predicted," said National Securities analyst Allen Huang.
Steel shares plunged 2.15 percent, with China Steel down 90 cents to T$29.3.
